summary: Signe Howell (1942–2025) was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. She studied at the University of Oxford from circa 1977 to 1980 and served as a professor at the University of Oslo from circa 1989 to 2012.
Sik Fanin works in Buddhist and religious studies. After earning a PhD from Lancaster University (circa 2003–2008), Sik held a teaching advisor post at the University of Hong Kong.

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. In Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at "L'Orientale," Sapienza University, Kyoto University of Foreign Studies, and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2002–2023).
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras from 2000 to 2014 and was Director of the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore.

Sisir Roy works in philosophy and other fields, having studied under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies.

Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Kwan studied under teacher Zhihua Yao and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong by 2010 under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.
So Takahashi is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo by 1973 and served as an associate professor at Meijo University until 1977.

Sodo Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as professor at Aichi Gakuin University, lecturer at Toyo and Taisho universities, and Japan representative for the Pali Text Society.
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under teachers Kodo Sawaki and Eiko Hashimoto, and later taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Shaku (1860–1919) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Kosen Imakita and at Keio University. He served as chief abbot at Engaku-ji in 1892 and held a post at Hanazono University.
Sogen Omori (1904–1994) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts at Kōho-in Temple from circa 1945 to 1994 and at Hanazono University from circa 1978 to 1982.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at Delhi and Cambridge, trained under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and founded Rigpa in 1975.

Soiku Shigematsu studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1961–1965) and under traditional teacher Kiju Shigematsu. Active in Buddhist studies and other fields, he held posts at Kansai Medical University and Shizuoka University (~1975–2008).
Sojo Hirano (1930–1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University and as shike at Zuigan-ji from circa 1979 to 1999.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetologist who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2003–2008). He held posts as a departmental lecturer at Oxford (~2012–2015) and as a researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who completed a PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (~1996–2000). He held posts at the Institut Français de Pondichéry, Oxford, Kyoto University (professor, 2011), and Columbia University (~2011–2013).

Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a Master's in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University by 2006, supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat with Watchara Ngamchitcharoen on his committee.

Sonam Chhoki is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University, completed a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.
